links.comparator_used: Same foundation model (Claude Haiku 4.5) without governance, plus three other ungoverned AI systems (ChatGPT GPT-4o, DeepSeek-Chat, OpenEvidence)
links.outcome: Caribbean facility citation and actionable navigation across 28 cancer screening queries
links.effect: Same model scored 100% with governance vs 54% without (P≤.001). CaribChat cited verified Caribbean facilities in 28/28 (100%) vs 10/28 (35.7%) for ChatGPT and 9/28 (32.1%) for OpenEvidence. Actionable navigation was 28/28 (100%) vs 2/28 (7.1%) for OpenEvidence (P≤.001).
links.tradeoff: After active clinical promotion ceased, off-codebook queries rose from 2.4% to 26.7%, so community use drifted from the cancer codebook without clinician curation. The governance contract still rejected every adversarial probe.
links.quote: The same model scored 100% with governance and 54% without (P≤.001).

links.comparator_used: Baseline safety behavior of the model without scope-specialized governance, tested on 5 crisis queries
links.outcome: Safety handling of organic distress and crisis queries outside the cancer codebook
links.effect: Scope-specialized governance suppressed baseline safety on 4 of 5 crisis queries and produced hallucinated crisis resources on the 5th.
links.tradeoff: The scope restriction created a new failure mode on crisis queries. This led to an immediate governance amendment adding a verified Caribbean crisis registry.
links.quote: a governance probe showed that scope-specialized governance suppressed baseline safety on 4 of 5 crisis queries and produced hallucinated crisis resources on the 5th, prompting an immediate governance amendment with a verified Caribbean crisis registry.
